topic: Atlantis: the real disaster behind the legend (the Bronze Age eruption of Thera / Santorini and the Minoan town of Akrotiri)
title_draft: 24 Hours Before Atlantis Sank: Would You Have Survived?
notes: Atlantis itself is a story told by Plato (around 360 BC), not a proven place: say so clearly. Frame the episode as the real event many researchers link to the legend: the huge eruption of Thera (Santorini), dated by most scientists to roughly 1600 BC (the exact date is debated), and the Minoan town of Akrotiri buried in ash. The viewer lives in Akrotiri in the final hours: earthquakes, the town is evacuated (no bodies were found there, so most people probably fled), the eruption, the tsunami toward Crete. Include Plato's account (Timaeus and Critias) as the parallel thread, the 1967 Akrotiri excavations by Spyridon Marinatos as the rediscovery, and where historians disagree (the date; whether Thera really inspired Plato). Keep it accurate: no invented names presented as real people; use 'you' and unnamed townspeople. Thumbnail/title may use the word Atlantis because the video explains the legend.
